community business in Scotland in the 198os and 199os was a movement that sought to address the problems of social and economic deprivation in Scotland through the development of a new model of business.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

community business was an alternative vision of enterprise culture that sought to address the problems of deindustrialisation by building on local resources and developing local solutions to local problems.

the community business movement, while sharing some similarities with Thatcherism, was an alternative vision for Scotland's economic and social development, one that was grounded in a community development ethos.
the community business movement provided a vision for a new form of community development that was rooted in the local community, but with a wider vision for social and economic development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown how community businesses in Scotland were a manifestation of an alternative vision of 'enterprise culture', and that the history of this movement provides an important signpost to an unrealized alternative for Scotland's future.

the movement's practitioners sought to build a new form of enterprise culture, which was rooted in community development and which sought to empower communities, to build local democracy, and to create new forms of economic and political power for communities.
we have shown that the community business movement was not just an attempt to 'fill the gaps left by the market and the state' (Hill 2001: 2) but an attempt to create a different kind of economy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the community business movement was an important part of the social and economic recovery of Scotland, and that it is a story worth telling.
the community business movement was not a simple response to the political and economic context of the 1970s and 1980s.
, although Thatcherism was a powerful force in the 198os, its influence was not absolute and that there were other visions for Scotland's future.
